answer: A registry blocks bulk fake identities by binding each identity to one physical enclave chip. Each epoch a public beacon publishes a fresh nonce the chip must sign. Its counter, driven by a quartz clock, advances once per signature and never rolls back. A chip signing for two identities exposes two counters on one key, so the registry stains both keys with pigment and slashes their deposits. The kth fake identity still needs a kth chip: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 chips at $40 each, $40,000 of hardware that cannot be shared, while an honest agent buys one chip once.
